newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour targets tax relief to fund VAT fuel cut.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour targets tax relief to fund VAT fuel cut.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party finance spokesman Gordon Brown said on Thursday he would scrap certain tax reliefs to slash VAT on domestic fuel if necessary.
Brown told BBC radio Labour's manifesto would show exactly how cutting fuel VAT would be funded. "It will include the tax relief on private medical insurance," he said.
He has pledged a Labour government would cut value-added-tax on fuel from 8 to 5 percent, financing it by scrapping the tax relief on private medical insurance for people over 60.
Cutting the VAT would cost 380 million in the first year, and 450 million in the second year, he said.

"It's a question of priority. The priority is getting VAT on fuel down," Brown said. "Most people would see that that helps everybody, whereas the tax relief for private medical insurance helps only a few."
Brown also warned the privatised utilities to accept his plans for a one-off levy on "excess" profits to finance schemes to tackle unemployment.
He said water companies had paid tax at an effective rate of only two percent on their profits, and in some cases none at all.
"That's one of the reasons why most people see it as fair to impose this windfall levy, to do something about a major social and economic problem."
Brown also defended Labour's decision not to vote against the budget's one penny income tax cut. "It would be wrong for us to vote against the tax cut."
